what:
Cursor 3.2.11 preToolUse:Read coverage gap — VERIFIED CAUSE 2026-04-27 18:05 UTC: **file-open-in-editor state bypasses the preToolUse:Read hook.** When a file is open in Cursor's editor pane, subsequent Read tool calls on that file do NOT fire the preToolUse hook. When the file is not open, preToolUse:Read fires reliably.

**Verification evidence (2026-04-27 18:04-18:06 UTC, brand-new file `src/utils/brand-new-file.ts`):**

| # | Session | Setup | Read tool? | preToolUse:Read fired? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 78a5e680 | Brand-new file, fresh chat (file NOT open in editor) | yes | ✅ YES (hard block) |
| 2 | e5298dd9 | Same file, fresh chat (file NOT open in editor) | yes | ✅ YES (hard block) |
| 3 | a1cbbd81 | Same file, fresh chat, **file PHYSICALLY OPENED in Cursor editor pane first** | yes | ❌ NO |

The ONLY variable between session 2 (fires) and session 3 (doesn't fire) was: user opened the file in the editor pane. Same fixture, same memories, same prompt, same agent tool_use shape. The hook's firing depends on Cursor's "is this file open in the editor?" state.

**Ruled out as causes:**
- ~~Input shape~~: same in all sessions
- ~~Cache cold/warm via repeated reads~~: brand-new file, only 3 reads total before opening it
- ~~Agent's preempting recall~~: tracking-file confirms no `file|<path>` entries from agent
- ~~Tool name mismatch~~: agent calls `Read`, our matcher matches, working sessions confirm

**Verified cause:** Cursor 3.2.11 likely has logic where files open in the editor pane have their content "served" to the agent without invoking the Read tool's preToolUse hook (probably to avoid latency / re-read of editor-managed content). The Read tool_use IS issued by the agent, but Cursor short-circuits the preToolUse pipeline.

**Coverage implication for 0.5.0 ship — IMPORTANT:**
- Per-Read hard-block fires when **file is NOT open in Cursor editor** (cold path)
- Per-Read hard-block bypassed when **file IS open in Cursor editor** (typical real-world workflow — users have files open while working)
- Per-Edit hard-block (preToolUse:Write) fires reliably regardless of editor-open state
- Practical impact: in real user workflows, the per-Read safety net often won't fire because users naturally have target files open. The per-Edit safety net is still load-bearing for any code-mutation flow.

**Documentation framing for cursor.md (per #351 + #358 + #363, all verified now):**
> aide-memory hard-blocks file edits when memories haven't been recalled. On Cursor 3.2.11:
> - Per-Edit hard-block fires reliably (every Write/Edit/StrReplace).
> - Per-Read hard-block fires only when the file is NOT open in Cursor's editor pane. When the file is open in the editor, Cursor serves content to the agent without invoking the preToolUse:Read hook — aide-memory's per-Read safety net is bypassed in this case.
> - Memory context still reaches the agent via the rules-file injection (`alwaysApply: true`), independent of hook firing.
> - The most reliable safety net for code edits is therefore the Edit hard-block, not the Read hard-block, in typical Cursor workflows.

**Possible workarounds for the Read coverage gap (Phase 1 follow-up candidates):**
1. Add `beforeReadFile` event registration alongside `preToolUse:Read` — beforeReadFile fires on file content access regardless of tool layer (pending empirical test). Caveat: forum #150520 says permission:deny on beforeReadFile isn't always honored — may not actually block.
2. File a Cursor FR to fire preToolUse:Read for editor-open files too.
3. Document and accept — practical impact mitigated by Edit hard-block + rules-file injection.

**For documentation: do NOT over-claim Read safety net reliability.** The honest claim is "Edits are reliably gated; Reads are best-effort and depend on Cursor editor state."

**Diagnostic methodology that worked:**
1. Cursor's transcript file at `~/.cursor/projects/<project-hash>/agent-transcripts/<session>/<session>.jsonl` — shows actual tool_use blocks
2. Run hook directly via `echo '<json>' | bash <hook-script>` — verifies hook code
3. Multiple repetitions on same configuration before drawing conclusions
4. **Vary one variable at a time** to isolate cause (e.g. open file in editor vs not)

**Methodology corrections from this session (don't repeat):**
- After ONE comparison I claimed "input-shape sensitivity" — wrong, retracted after multi-trial
- After multi-trial I claimed cache theory was "verified" — wrong, that was hypothesis
- Now (after isolating editor-open variable): editor-open-state cause is empirically VERIFIED with controlled experiment. This is the actual answer.
why: User ran the controlled experiment that isolated the cause: brand-new file, two sessions identical except one had the file opened in editor first. The hook fires when file isn't open, doesn't fire when it is. This IS verified — a controlled experiment with single variable change. Updating memory from "hypothesis" to "verified" with proper evidence chain. The implications for 0.5.0 ship are now concrete and documentable honestly.
